note: Names, descriptions and grades are the official PlayStation list as published on Exophase and PSNProfiles. Hidden flags follow PSN's list. Counts (such as 42 Shooting Range challenges) are the targets PSN tracks, as listed on PSNProfiles. Every guide below is written for this entry, in our own words, and cites its sources beside it.

trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!
trophies.guide: The platinum is the last trophy you earn, not the first: it pops the moment the other 54 are done. There is no shortcut and no single trick to it — work the roadmap in order (story first, then strangers and activities, then collectibles, then money and cleanup) and this one takes care of itself. If you are reading this guide at the start, tick off the missable story trophies as they come, because those are the only ones that can cost you a second playthrough.
trophies.sources: Sources: official trophy list on Exophase for the name, description and grade; PSNProfiles for the tracked counts; our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Just Like Paradise
trophies.guide: Play the opening mission, Gone Fishing, to its end. It is the game's first story mission, so you cannot skip past it — finish it and the trophy pops. It is flagged missable here only because it is tied to one story moment: if you ever replay the story, earn it on your first run through the mission and do not leave it half-finished.
trophies.sources: Sources: official trophy list on Exophase for the name, description and grade; our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Paradise Lost
trophies.guide: Finish every story mission in Chapter 1. Chapters end when the last mission of the chapter is complete, so keep playing the main story and this pops on its own. It is flagged missable because it belongs to one chapter: if the game lets you replay missions, you can recover it, but do not assume that — clear the chapter the first time through.
trophies.sources: Sources: official trophy list on Exophase for the name, description and grade; our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money
trophies.guide: Finish every story mission in Chapter 2. Like the other chapter trophies, this one comes from playing the main story to the chapter's end, and it is flagged missable for the same reason: it is tied to one chapter, so clear it on your first run through rather than counting on mission replay.
trophies.sources: Sources: official trophy list on Exophase for the name, description and grade; our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!
trophies.guide: Finish every story mission in Chapter 3. The chapter trophies are the spine of the roadmap: play the story in order, and each one pops as its chapter closes. Flagged missable because it is bound to a single chapter — finish the chapter before moving on to side content that might pull you away for hours.
trophies.sources: Sources: official trophy list on Exophase for the name, description and grade; our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma
trophies.guide: Finish every story mission in Chapter 4. This is the last chapter trophy before the finale, so by the time it pops you are one step from the gold for the final mission. Same rule as the other chapters: clear it on your first run through the chapter.
trophies.sources: Sources: official trophy list on Exophase for the name, description and grade; our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off
trophies.guide: Finish the final story mission. This is the gold that closes the campaign, and it only pops once — if the finale branches or offers a choice, save before it so you can see the other branch without a second full playthrough. The official description names no mission title, so the finale's name is deliberately left out of this guide to avoid spoiling it.
trophies.sources: Sources: official trophy list on Exophase for the name, description and grade; our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Trust
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Breakfast Run. Named-mission trophies like this one are the ones to watch: each belongs to a single mission, so play it through to the end and let the trophy pop before you move on. If you fail the mission, retry it immediately rather than leaving it for later.
trophies.sources: Sources: official trophy list on Exophase for the name, description and grade; our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Break the Bank
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission The Cartel Heist. Heist missions are usually the long, multi-stage ones, so give this one a full session: finish every stage of the heist in one run and the trophy pops at the end. Flagged missable because it is tied to that one mission.
trophies.sources: Sources: official trophy list on Exophase for the name, description and grade; our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Family Matters
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Child's Play. Like every named-mission trophy, this one is earned by playing that mission to completion — nothing extra to do, no collectible to find first. Do it on your first run through the mission and tick it off.
trophies.sources: Sources: official trophy list on Exophase for the name, description and grade; our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: DWNFALL
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Headliners. The mission's name hints at a public, high-profile job, so expect a set-piece rather than a quiet errand — but the trophy itself asks only that you finish the mission. Play it through to the end on your first attempt at it.
trophies.sources: Sources: official trophy list on Exophase for the name, description and grade; our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Hi-Jacked
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission VCIA Takedown, set at Vice City International Airport. This is one of two airport trophies — the other, Catch Me If You Can, is about leaving the airport in an unscheduled way — so if you are at VCIA for this mission, remember the second one too. Finish the mission and the trophy pops.
trophies.sources: Sources: official trophy list on Exophase for the name, description and grade; our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Snow Storm
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Operation Savage Glory. The name suggests a big military-style operation, so stock up before you start it and play it through in one go. As with every named-mission trophy, finishing the mission is the whole requirement.
trophies.sources: Sources: official trophy list on Exophase for the name, description and grade; our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: A Long Road
trophies.guide: Reach 100% completion in the game's own checklist. This is the gold that sits behind everything else: story, stranger strands, collectibles, activities and the rest all feed into it, so it pops last, just before the platinum. Do not chase it early — use this guide's roadmap and the in-game 100% list, and treat every other trophy as a step toward this one. It cannot be missed, only left unfinished.
trophies.sources: Sources: official trophy list on Exophase for the name, description and grade; our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Cunning Stunts
trophies.guide: Pull off 250 stunts across Leonida — jumps, near misses, long air time and the rest all count toward the same total. This is a grind trophy, not a skill gate: it accumulates over the whole game, so drive fast, take ramps and jump gaps whenever you see them and you will pass 250 long before the platinum. Track it in this guide's checklist and check the in-game counter when you want a number.
trophies.sources: Sources: official trophy list on Exophase for the name, description and grade; PSNProfiles for the tracked count of 250; our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Master of None
trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: Try one of every activity type the game offers, once each. The official description does not list the types or say how many there are, so work through the activities menu and the map icons one by one — racing, fishing, shooting range, drone races, arcade games, bowling and the rest — and tick each off here as you try it. This is a sampler, not a mastery trophy: one attempt at each is enough.
trophies.sources: Sources: official trophy list on Exophase for the name, description and grade; our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: The Shootist
trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: Earn a gold medal in all 42 Shooting Range challenges. This is the first real skill gate on the list, so take it in short sessions rather than in one sitting: learn each range's targets and timing, use the steadiest weapon you own, and replay the challenges you miss until every one shows gold. The count of 42 is the target PSN tracks, so this guide's checklist shows it beside the trophy.
trophies.sources: Sources: official trophy list on Exophase for the name, description and grade; PSNProfiles for the tracked count of 42 challenges; our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Top Fun
trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: Win a Top Fun drone race at every one of the 14 locations. Drone races are a flying skill check: learn each course's line before you race it for real, cut corners only where the gates allow it, and win once at each location — you do not need to win every race, only one at each of the 14 spots. The count of 14 locations is the target PSN tracks.
trophies.sources: Sources: official trophy list on Exophase for the name, description and grade; PSNProfiles for the tracked count of 14 locations; our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos
trophies.guide: Win 20 different races. Different is the word that matters: winning the same race twenty times does not count, so work through the race list and win a new one each time. Short, easy races count the same as long ones, so pick the shortest courses first and bank twenty wins across the map.
trophies.sources: Sources: official trophy list on Exophase for the name, description and grade; PSNProfiles for the tracked count of 20; our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Baited My Tackle
trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.guide: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge. Cal is a named rival, so this is a duel rather than a free fishing session: take the challenge when it appears, and fish the way the challenge scores it — the right spot, the right bait and steady reeling beat rushing. If you lose, the challenge can be retried, so keep at it until Cal is beaten.
trophies.sources: Sources: official trophy list on Exophase for the name, description and grade; our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Stick Fiddler
trophies.guide: Complete one arcade game, start to finish. Any arcade machine counts and any game on it counts, so pick the shortest or easiest one you find and play it through once. This is one of the quickest trophies on the list — do it the first time you pass an arcade.
trophies.sources: Sources: official trophy list on Exophase for the name, description and grade; our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Road to Rehabilitation
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Andy.
trophies.guide: Complete Andy's final mission. Each named character has a strand of side missions that ends in one last job, and this trophy is Andy's: play his missions in order until the final one appears, then finish it. It is flagged missable because it belongs to one mission — do not leave Andy's strand half-done when you move to the endgame.
trophies.sources: Sources: official trophy list on Exophase for the name, description and grade; our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: This Was No Boat Accident
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Kenton.
trophies.guide: Complete Kenton's final mission. Kenton's strand ends on the water, judging by the trophy's name, so expect a boat job for the finale — but the trophy only asks that you finish the mission. Play Kenton's missions in order and clear the last one when it unlocks.
trophies.sources: Sources: official trophy list on Exophase for the name, description and grade; our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: The Lone Rider
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Billy.
trophies.guide: Complete Billy's final mission. Billy's strand is the lone-rider one, so expect a solo bike job for the finale. As with the other character strands, play his missions in order and finish the last one when it appears — flagged missable because it is tied to that single mission.
trophies.sources: Sources: official trophy list on Exophase for the name, description and grade; our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Strangers & Freaks
trophies.description: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.
trophies.guide: Complete 8 stranger mission strands across Leonida. Strangers appear as question marks on the map: talk to them, take their jobs and follow each strand to its end. Eight strands is the count PSN tracks, and there are more strangers than eight in the state, so you can skip the ones you dislike and still finish. Do these as you explore, not in one late grind.
trophies.sources: Sources: official trophy list on Exophase for the name, description and grade; PSNProfiles for the tracked count of 8 strands; our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Supply & Demand
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Randy.
trophies.guide: Complete Randy's final mission. Randy's strand is the supply one, so expect jobs about moving goods — play his missions in order until the last one unlocks, then finish it. Flagged missable because it belongs to that one final mission.
trophies.sources: Sources: official trophy list on Exophase for the name, description and grade; our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Spin On This!
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Tyrone.
trophies.guide: Complete Tyrone's final mission. Tyrone's strand ends in one last job — play his missions in order and clear the finale when it appears. Like the other character strands, it is flagged missable because it is tied to a single mission, so do not put it off until after the story ends.
trophies.sources: Sources: official trophy list on Exophase for the name, description and grade; our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude
trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.guide: Meditate at all 18 meditation spots across Leonida. The spots are spread over the whole map, so treat this as an exploration trophy: visit each one, sit down and meditate, and tick it off here. The count of 18 is the target PSN tracks — if you are stuck on the last few, work through the map region by region rather than driving at random.
trophies.sources: Sources: official trophy list on Exophase for the name, description and grade; PSNProfiles for the tracked count of 18 spots; our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Fair Game
trophies.description: Hunt a unique animal for Bret.
trophies.guide: Hunt a unique animal for Bret. Bret's job is a hunting one: find the animal he names, track it and take it down cleanly. The official description does not name the animal or the place, so this guide does not invent either — take Bret's job, follow his directions in the game, and use a scoped rifle and a quiet approach rather than chasing the animal on foot.
trophies.sources: Sources: official trophy list on Exophase for the name, description and grade; our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Don't Touch My Deck
trophies.guide: Complete 3 collectible card sets. Cards are scattered across Leonida, and a set is only done when every card in it is found — so collect in sets, not at random, and finish three whole sets before you move on. Three sets is the count PSN tracks; there are more sets in the game, so pick the three whose cards you find first.
trophies.sources: Sources: official trophy list on Exophase for the name, description and grade; PSNProfiles for the tracked count of 3 sets; our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: You WAiNKer!
trophies.guide: Use the WAiNK It feature at 100 different locations. This is a long grind — one hundred spots — so do it as you travel, not as a separate hunt: open WAiNK It whenever you arrive somewhere new and the count climbs on its own. The official description does not list the locations, so work the map region by region and let this guide's progress counter keep the running total.
trophies.sources: Sources: official trophy list on Exophase for the name, description and grade; PSNProfiles for the tracked count of 100 locations; our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: One Last Thing
trophies.guide: Complete 50 challenges. Challenges are the game's small side goals — the kind that tick off as you play — so this one accumulates naturally over a full playthrough. If you reach the endgame short of 50, open the challenges menu, pick the easiest unfinished ones and clear them in a batch. Fifty is the count PSN tracks.
trophies.sources: Sources: official trophy list on Exophase for the name, description and grade; PSNProfiles for the tracked count of 50; our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Hot Together
trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.guide: With your partner beside you, build a 4-star wanted level and then lose it and escape. Do it somewhere you can run: earn the stars with your partner in the car or on foot, then break line of sight, get out of the search area and stay hidden until the stars clear. It is flagged missable because it needs your partner with you — do it during a story stretch where your partner is around, not after the finale.
trophies.sources: Sources: official trophy list on Exophase for the name, description and grade; our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Retail Therapy
trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.guide: With your partner, rob 3 shops back to back without ever losing your wanted level. The trick is the opposite of Hot Together: here you must keep the heat the whole time, so rob one shop, drive straight to the next and rob it while the stars are still up, then the third — do not stop, do not hide, and do not let the stars clear between robberies. Plan a route of three close shops before you start, and do it while your partner is available.
trophies.sources: Sources: official trophy list on Exophase for the name, description and grade; our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Whip It Good
trophies.guide: Discover 100 different vehicles. A vehicle counts when you first get in or spot it — so drive everything you see, from beat-up sedans to rare rides, and the count climbs fast. One hundred is the target PSN tracks; the rarest vehicles are the ones to hunt last, and this guide's checklist is where you track which kinds you still need.
trophies.sources: Sources: official trophy list on Exophase for the name, description and grade; PSNProfiles for the tracked count of 100; our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Gunslinger
trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.guide: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus. Set it up rather than hoping for it: find a fight with a group of enemies close together, trigger Combat Focus when they are bunched up, and drop five before it runs out. A crowded street fight or a gang shootout is the place to try it — and if you only get four, reload the attempt and try again.
trophies.sources: Sources: official trophy list on Exophase for the name, description and grade; our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can
trophies.description: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.
trophies.guide: Make an unscheduled departure at Vice City International Airport — in plain words, steal a plane and take off without a flight plan. Get onto the airfield, grab a plane and get it into the air; the trophy is about the departure, not the destination. It is flagged missable because it is a one-off moment at the airport: do it the first time you are at VCIA with a free moment, and expect the police to notice.
trophies.sources: Sources: official trophy list on Exophase for the name, description and grade; our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Challenging Tank
trophies.guide: This one is about the Rhino tank, and the official description is a joke, not an instruction — it does not say what to do with one. The honest reading: get into a Rhino and use it, most likely at high wanted levels where the army rolls them out. Steal one when it appears, drive it and cause chaos with it until the trophy pops, and if it does not, try surviving in one through a wanted level instead. No location is pinned down here because the description pins none down — and a guide that claimed one would be guessing.
trophies.sources: Sources: official trophy list on Exophase for the name, description and grade; our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Sneakthief
trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.guide: Rob a jewelry store without being detected. Stealth is the whole job: go in quiet, avoid the cameras and the staff's line of sight, take the goods and leave before anyone raises the alarm. If you are spotted, the attempt fails — leave, lose the heat and try again, or reload a save from before you entered. Pick a small store for your first try.
trophies.sources: Sources: official trophy list on Exophase for the name, description and grade; our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal
trophies.guide: Rob 5 bank vaults and escape from each one. Vaults are the big robberies: plan the getaway before the break-in, use a fast car parked close, and escape cleanly after each vault — a vault that ends in a bust does not count. Five vaults is the count PSN tracks, so space them out across the game rather than doing all five in one session.
trophies.sources: Sources: official trophy list on Exophase for the name, description and grade; PSNProfiles for the tracked count of 5; our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: A Classic Blitz Play
trophies.description: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.
trophies.guide: Rob an armored truck and escape. Armored trucks drive set routes around the map: find one, stop it — block the road or shoot out its tires — take the cash and get away before the police box you in. It is a one-and-done trophy, so pick a quiet stretch of road for the ambush and have a fast getaway car ready.
trophies.sources: Sources: official trophy list on Exophase for the name, description and grade; our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: The Goodtime State
trophies.guide: Explore all 52 areas of Leonida. This is the map-completion trophy: visit every named area of the state, from Vice City's districts to the far corners of the map, and the trophy pops when the last one is discovered. Drive the whole map in a sweep, region by region, and use this guide's progress counter to track the areas you still need — 52 is the target PSN tracks.
trophies.sources: Sources: official trophy list on Exophase for the name, description and grade; PSNProfiles for the tracked count of 52 areas; our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Pest Control
trophies.description: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang.
trophies.guide: Rob an illegal operation belonging to each of the 9 gangs. Every gang in Leonida runs operations you can hit — rob one operation per gang, all nine, and the trophy pops. Keep a list of which gangs you have hit and which you have not; the count of 9 gangs is the target PSN tracks, so the last gang is the one to hunt deliberately.
trophies.sources: Sources: official trophy list on Exophase for the name, description and grade; PSNProfiles for the tracked count of 9 gangs; our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: In The Beginning…
trophies.description: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.
trophies.guide: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach. This one is a breather, not a challenge: go to Ocean Beach, find a bar or spot with a view over the water, and order a cocktail. It pops when you drink it in the right place — the official description names Ocean Beach, so that is the only location this guide can pin down, and it is the one that matters.
trophies.sources: Sources: official trophy list on Exophase for the name, description and grade; our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Capital Offense
trophies.description: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style.
trophies.guide: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style — drive a car straight through the showroom's glass front, the way the old games did it. Pick a showroom, get a car inside or lined up at the window, and floor it through the glass. It is flagged missable because it is tied to one showroom moment: do it the first time you are in a showroom with a car, and save before you try in case the attempt goes wrong.
trophies.sources: Sources: official trophy list on Exophase for the name, description and grade; our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Let’s Go Bowling
trophies.description: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
trophies.guide: Play bowling at the Kolt & Associates bowling alley. The official description names the alley, so this one has a real address: go to Kolt & Associates, rent a lane and bowl a game — follow through on the throw and finish the game. It is a quiet activity trophy, so do it between story missions when you want a break.
trophies.sources: Sources: official trophy list on Exophase for the name, description and grade; our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Personal Best
trophies.guide: This is the vaguest trophy on the list: the official description says only that it is a partnership with mass appeal. The honest reading is that it is tied to your partner and to reaching a wide audience — most likely the in-game social media following you build together. Keep playing the partner content, grow the following, and it should pop; this guide does not invent a number or a place for it because the description gives neither.
trophies.sources: Sources: official trophy list on Exophase for the name, description and grade; our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Actions Speak Louder
trophies.guide: Make choices — for better or worse. PSN tracks a count to 500 for this one, so it is about the volume of decisions you make across the game, not one big choice. Play naturally, take the dialogue and story choices as they come, and the count climbs; if you reach the endgame short of 500, replay choice-heavy missions and pick the other option. It is flagged missable only in the sense that choices are made once — save before the big ones so you can see both sides.
trophies.sources: Sources: official trophy list on Exophase for the name, description and grade; PSNProfiles for the tracked count of 500; our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Bad Luck, I Guess
trophies.guide: Succeed on a second try. The description is a riddle, but the reading is plain: fail something once, then succeed at it the second time. It will most likely pop on its own during a normal playthrough — a failed mission, a lost race, a missed shot, then a clean second attempt. Do not chase it deliberately at first; if it has not popped by the endgame, fail a short activity once on purpose and then win it.
trophies.sources: Sources: official trophy list on Exophase for the name, description and grade; our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: The Truth Is Out There
trophies.guide: Witness something strange. This is the game's mystery trophy — the description is a reaction, not an instruction — and it will be about a random or hidden event in the world, the kind players share clips of. Explore the odd corners of Leonida, follow strange map markers and pay attention to night-time events; this guide does not name the event because the description does not, and the community will pin it down first.
trophies.sources: Sources: official trophy list on Exophase for the name, description and grade; our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Ten Pin
trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.guide: Knock someone over with a melee drive-by — hit a pedestrian with a melee weapon from a moving vehicle. Drive slowly through a crowded street, lean out and swing as you pass. It is a grim little stunt, so do it once, get the trophy and move on; a slow car and a straight street make the aim easy.
trophies.sources: Sources: official trophy list on Exophase for the name, description and grade; our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Dime on the Dollar
trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.guide: Earn $250,000 by laundering marked bills through your contacts. Marked bills come from robberies and heists, and your contacts clean them for a cut — so keep robbing, keep laundering, and the total climbs. Two hundred and fifty thousand is the target PSN tracks; treat it as a background goal while you work the robbery trophies, and it will finish around the same time as Maximum Withdrawal.
trophies.sources: Sources: official trophy list on Exophase for the name, description and grade; PSNProfiles for the tracked count of $250,000; our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Treat Yo Self
trophies.guide: Spend $100,000 across all shops. Every dollar you spend in any shop counts toward the same total, so buy the clothes, weapons, cars and upgrades you actually want and the number climbs on its own. One hundred thousand is the target PSN tracks — by the endgame you will have spent most of it without trying, and a car purchase or two closes the gap.
trophies.sources: Sources: official trophy list on Exophase for the name, description and grade; PSNProfiles for the tracked count of $100,000; our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Little Boxes
trophies.guide: Purchase all 8 garage properties. Garages are bought from the property listings as they unlock: buy each one when it appears, and keep this guide's checklist open so you know which of the eight you still need. Eight is the count PSN tracks, and the last garage is usually the most expensive, so save your money for it late in the game.
trophies.sources: Sources: official trophy list on Exophase for the name, description and grade; PSNProfiles for the tracked count of 8 properties; our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: On the Spot
trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app. Find vehicles you like, bring them to the app and register them — ten different ones is the target PSN tracks. It pairs naturally with Whip It Good, so register the interesting cars you discover as you go and this one finishes alongside the vehicle hunt.
trophies.sources: Sources: official trophy list on Exophase for the name, description and grade; PSNProfiles for the tracked count of 10; our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.
